summary: binding.gyp abuses gyp Python-eval to execute obfuscated sibling payload on install
details: The tarball ships a binding.gyp whose `conditions` clause is not a legitimate gyp expression but a Python sandbox-escape (`().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()` → `catch_warnings` → `__builtins__.__import__('os').system(...)`), whose unicode-escaped command decodes to `node 3FWCvzduYZg.js`. Because npm invokes node-gyp for any package containing a binding.gyp, this fires automatically during `npm install`. The invoked sibling `3FWCvzduYZg.js` is a ~5.6MB file consisting of a single `Function(charcodes.map(c => String.fromCharCode(c^88)).join(''))()` call over character-code data that decodes to ~1.6MB of opaque JavaScript, dynamically constructed and executed at install time. The sibling file is not declared in package.json (`"files": ["dist"]`) yet is shipped at the tarball root under a random name alongside the weaponized binding.gyp, indicating the payload is smuggled outside the author's declared publish surface — consistent with a maintainer/namespace compromise rather than a normal release of the codegen tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
